items.articleText: Akbank'tan COP31'de sürdürülebilir finans mesajı: İşletmelerin dönüşümüne destek - Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür, COP31 kapsamında düzenlenen panelde iklim dönüşümünde finans sektörünün rolüne dikkat çekti. Gür, Sürdürülebilir İklimlendirme Finansman Programı ile işletmelerin enerji verimliliği yatırımlarını ve düşük karbonlu ekonomiye geçişini desteklediklerini belirtti. Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür, COP31 kapsamında UNDP tarafından düzenlenen üst düzey panelde Türkiye’nin Ulusal Soğutma Eylem Planı’nın uygulanmasında finans sektörünün rolünü değerlendirdi. Gür, Akbank’ın Sürdürülebilir İklimlendirme Finansman Programı ile işletmelerin daha verimli sistemlere geçişini ve uluslararası kaynaklarla Türkiye’deki yatırım önceliklerinin buluşturulmasını desteklediklerini belirtti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür, BM İklim Değişikliği Çerçeve Sözleşmesi 31. Taraflar Konferansı (COP31) kapsamında, Birleşmiş Milletler Kalkınma Programı (UNDP) tarafından düzenlenen “Kamu-Özel Sektör İş Birliği ve Sürdürülebilir Finans Yoluyla Türkiye’nin Ulusal Soğutma Eylem Planı’nın Uygulanmasının Hızlandırılması” başlıklı panele katıldı. Moderatörlüğünü UNDP Türkiye Mukim Temsilci Yardımcısı Tomica Paović’in üstlendiği; konuşmacılar arasında T.C. Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakanlığı İklim Değişikliği Başkanlığı Başkan Yardımcısı Mehrali Ecer, UNDP Türkiye İklim Değişikliği ve Çevre Portföy Yöneticisi Meral Mungan Arda, Guidehouse Direktörü Katja Eisbrenner ile İklimlendirme Soğutma Klima İmalatçıları Derneği Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Süleyman Kavas’ın da yer aldığı panelde, Türkiye’nin soğutma alanındaki önceliklerinin uygulanabilir ve ölçeklenebilir projelere dönüştürülmesi konusu ele alındı. Konuya ilişkin yaptığı açıklamada Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür, “Soğutma sistemlerinin verimliliği, emisyonların azaltılmasının yanında işletmelerin maliyetlerini ve faaliyetlerini sürdürme gücünü de doğrudan etkiliyor. Türkiye’nin Ulusal Soğutma Eylem Planı bu alanda ülkemizin yönünü ve dönüşüm stratejisini belirliyor. Önceliğimiz, plandaki hedefleri işletmelerin hayata geçirebileceği yatırımlara dönüştürmek olmalı. Bankalar, geniş müşteri ağları sayesinde öncelikli sektörleri ve yatırım ihtiyaçlarını sahada belirleyebilir; işletmelerin uygun teknolojilere ve gerekli teknik yetkinliklere erişimini destekleyebilir. Mevcut sürdürülebilir finansman ürünlerini bu yatırımlarla buluştururken, kalkınma kuruluşları ve teknoloji uzmanlarıyla iş birlikleri kurabilir. Böylece enerji tasarrufunu, emisyon azaltımını ve ekonomik getiriyi görünür hâle getirerek işletmelerin yatırım kararlarını kolaylaştırabilir ve daha verimli sistemlere geçişi hızlandırabilir. Bu doğrultuda Akbank olarak sürdürülebilir iklimlendirme yatırımlarını daha kolay belirlenen, ölçülen ve finanse edilen bir yapıya kavuşturmak için çalışıyoruz. Cool Up Programı’nın Türkiye’deki ilk finansal partneri olarak hayata geçirdiğimiz Sürdürülebilir İklimlendirme Finansman Programımızla bu süreci destekliyoruz. Amacımız, uluslararası kaynaklarla Türkiye’deki yatırım önceliklerini buluşturarak daha verimli sistemlere geçişi kolaylaştırmak ve ekonominin iklim değişikliğine karşı dayanıklılığını artırmak” dedi.

items.articleText: Maliyet hesabı şaşırttı: Benzin ve motorine fiyatları elektrikli araçlara talebi artırdı - İngiltere'de benzin ve motorin fiyatlarındaki artış elektrikli otomobil satışlarını destekledi. Ancak beş farklı model üzerinden yapılan karşılaştırma, elektrikli araçların evde şarj edilse bile her zaman daha düşük maliyet sunmadığını, hızlı şarjda ise avantajın çoğunlukla kaybolduğunu gösterdi. ABD ile İran arasındaki çatışmanın etkisiyle İngiltere'de akaryakıt fiyatlarının yükselmesi, sürücülerin elektrikli otomobillere yönelmesini hızlandırdı. Ancak yeni araçlardaki indirimler ve şarj maliyetleri dikkate alındığında elektrikli otomobil tercihinin her durumda daha ekonomik olmadığı ortaya çıktı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Daily Mail'in haberine göre, İngiltere'de benzin fiyatları şubat ayına kıyasla litre başına yaklaşık 41 peni, motorin fiyatları ise 57 peni arttı. Bu artış, 55 litrelik bir deponun doldurulma maliyetini benzinli araçlarda yaklaşık 23 sterlin, dizel araçlarda 32 sterlin yükseltti. Akaryakıt maliyetlerindeki artış, elektrikli araçlara olan talebi de destekledi. Ocak-ekim döneminde yeni benzinli otomobil satışları yıllık yüzde 4,4 düşerek yaklaşık 35 bin 600 adet azalırken, dizel araç satışları yüzde 7,8 gerileyerek 83 bin 500'e indi. Tam elektrikli araç satışları yüzde 30,4, şarj edilebilir hibrit satışları ise yüzde 40 arttı. İngiliz Otomobil Birliği AA'nın Elektrikli Araçlara Hazırlık Endeksi'ne göre, elektrikli otomobile geçmeyi değerlendiren sürücülerin oranı 100 üzerinden 60'a yükseldi. Bu oran bir yıldan biraz daha uzun süre önce 47,5 seviyesindeydi. Benzinli ve dizel araçlarda indirimler azaldı Araç satışlarındaki gerilemeye rağmen bayilerin benzinli ve dizel modellerde indirimleri artırmak yerine azalttığı görüldü. Insider Car Deals verilerine göre, yeni benzinli otomobillerde ortalama indirim şubat ayındaki yüzde 10,8 seviyesinden kasımda yüzde 10,2'ye geriledi. Dizel araçlardaki indirim oranı da aynı dönemde yüzde 9,7'den yüzde 8,5'e düştü. Hibrit otomobillerde indirimler yüzde 11,3 seviyesinde sabit kalırken, elektrikli araçlardaki ortalama indirim oranı yıl başındaki yüzde 13 seviyesinden yüzde 11,1'e indi. Elektrikli araç her zaman daha ucuz değil Insider Car Deals, beş farklı araç çiftini karşılaştırarak elektrikli ve içten yanmalı motorlu modellerin aylık maliyetlerini inceledi. Hesaplamalarda yıllık 7 bin mil (yaklaşık 11 bin 265 kilometre) kullanım, araçların PCP finansman ödemeleri ve yakıt veya şarj giderleri dikkate alındı. Evde düşük tarifeli elektrikle şarj edilen araçlarda bile beş karşılaştırmanın yalnızca üçünde elektrikli model daha düşük aylık maliyet sundu. Halka açık hızlı şarj istasyonlarının kullanılması durumunda ise elektrikli araçların maliyet avantajı çoğunlukla ortadan kalktı.

Bu artış, 55 litrelik bir deponun doldurulma maliyetini benzinli araçlarda yaklaşık 23 sterlin, dizel araçlarda 32 sterlin yükseltti. Akaryakıt maliyetlerindeki artış, elektrikli araçlara olan talebi de destekledi. Ocak-ekim döneminde yeni benzinli otomobil satışları yıllık yüzde 4,4 düşerek yaklaşık 35 bin 600 adet azalırken, dizel araç satışları yüzde 7,8 gerileyerek 83 bin 500'e indi. Tam elektrikli araç satışları yüzde 30,4, şarj edilebilir hibrit satışları ise yüzde 40 arttı. İngiliz Otomobil Birliği AA'nın Elektrikli Araçlara Hazırlık Endeksi'ne göre, elektrikli otomobile geçmeyi değerlendiren sürücülerin oranı 100 üzerinden 60'a yükseldi. Bu oran bir yıldan biraz daha uzun süre önce 47,5 seviyesindeydi. Benzinli ve dizel araçlarda indirimler azaldı Araç satışlarındaki gerilemeye rağmen bayilerin benzinli ve dizel modellerde indirimleri artırmak yerine azalttığı görüldü. Insider Car Deals verilerine göre, yeni benzinli otomobillerde ortalama indirim şubat ayındaki yüzde 10,8 seviyesinden kasımda yüzde 10,2'ye geriledi. Dizel araçlardaki indirim oranı da aynı dönemde yüzde 9,7'den yüzde 8,5'e düştü. Hibrit otomobillerde indirimler yüzde 11,3 seviyesinde sabit kalırken, elektrikli araçlardaki ortalama indirim oranı yıl başındaki yüzde 13 seviyesinden yüzde 11,1'e indi. Elektrikli araç her zaman daha ucuz değil Insider Car Deals, beş farklı araç çiftini karşılaştırarak elektrikli ve içten yanmalı motorlu modellerin aylık maliyetlerini inceledi. Hesaplamalarda yıllık 7 bin mil (yaklaşık 11 bin 265 kilometre) kullanım, araçların PCP finansman ödemeleri ve yakıt veya şarj giderleri dikkate alındı. Evde düşük tarifeli elektrikle şarj edilen araçlarda bile beş karşılaştırmanın yalnızca üçünde elektrikli model daha düşük aylık maliyet sundu. Halka açık hızlı şarj istasyonlarının kullanılması durumunda ise elektrikli araçların maliyet avantajı çoğunlukla ortadan kalktı.

items.titleTr: Indonesia's vice-president resigns amid signs ruling alliance is fraying
items.summaryTr: The news comes at a turbulent time for President Prabowo, who faces a growing rift with his predecessor Joko Widodo.
items.articleText: Indonesia's vice-president resigns amid signs ruling alliance is fraying - Published Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka tendered his resignation to parliament on Thursday, triggering the process of finding his replacement amid growing turmoil for the government. Gibran had been facing impeachment calls after a Supreme Court ruling that a high-school document used during his 2024 election campaign was invalid. His departure comes amid a faltering political alliance between his father, ex-president Joko Widodo, and the incumbent President Prabowo Subianto. Standing alongside Gibran, Prabowo told reporters he had accepted his resignation with "a heavy heart". Upper house lawmakers will have 60 days to fill the vacancy from two candidates nominated by the president. "[Gibran] has demonstrated a chivalrous attitude, a strong sense of responsibility, and the qualities of a statesman," Prabowo said, adding that the resignation was "for the benefit of the nation, the state, and the people of Indonesia". "He certainly believes that he completed his education through a proper and structured process. However, we must understand that educational systems abroad differ from those in Indonesia," the president said. Gibran has long faced controversy over whether his high school qualifications met legal requirements to run for office. Having studied in Singapore and Australia, he had used an Indonesian equivalence certificate to demonstrate his educational credentials. Indonesian law requires vice-presidents to have completed senior secondary school or its equivalent, but the Supreme Court found no evidence to prove Gibran had graduated. "No evidence was found to show Gibran had a foreign diploma or certificate that could serve as the basis for equivalency with a senior high school or equivalent qualification," it said. It also considered a Constitutional Court ruling from earlier in October which came to the same conclusion. The Supreme Court ruling prompted more than 100 lawmakers to support a parliamentary initiative that could have paved the way for proceedings to impeach Gibran. Gibran previously argued that undertaking university education was sufficient proof that he had completed senior high school. On Tuesday, he asked for the chance to challenge the ruling and be given the opportunity to prove the legitimacy of his education credentials, State Secretariat Prasetyo Hadi said. Gibran's ascension to Prabowo's ticket in the 2024 election was part of an alliance formed between his father, outgoing president Joko Widodo - known as Jokowi - and Prabowo, his erstwhile bitter rival. Gibran was 36 at the time, and only became eligible for candidacy after a controversial ruling by the Constitutional Court, which exempted him from the minimum age requirement of 40. But tensions between Jokowi and Prabowo appear to have flared. Since taking the presidency, Prabowo has shown little interest in pushing ahead with Jokowi's legacy project: the construction of Nusantara, a new capital. Instead, he has focused much of the state's resources on his own flagship programme to provide free school meals across the country. In a series of personnel reshuffles over the past year, Prabowo has also shifted many Jokowi loyalists into new roles, including long-serving finance minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati. Last week, authorities arrested several senior officials, including presidential chief of staff Listyo Sigit Prabowo - no relation to Prabowo - on suspicions of wiretapping the president. Prabowo sacked Listyo a day later, in what many pointed to as a sign of a crumbling alliance: Listyo, who formerly served as the national police chief, is widely considered a long-time ally of Jokowi. Within the government, allegiances seem to be shifting. On Monday, three members of Prabowo's cabinet collectively resigned from the party led by Kaesang Pangarep, Jokowi's youngest son, citing their desire to focus on their duties in Prabowo's administration. But neither man has confirmed the rift. Speaking to reporters on Thursday, Jokowi said he still supported Prabowo's leadership. Jokowi also said Gibran's resignation was part of "political dynamics" and he had told his son "the position was temporary". All this is unfolding at a particularly turbulent period in Prabowo's presidency. The free school meals programme is struggling for funding, parts of Indonesia have recently battled the country's worst wildfires in a decade, and the national stock market faces crisis amid allegations of widespread market manipulation. Across the country, students and activists have staged demonstrations to protest against the government's handling of a range of issues, including the environmental crisis and corruption. items.titleTr: BlackRock Bitcoin ETF outflows hit $2B over nine sessions
items.summaryTr: US spot Bitcoin ETF outflows rose to nearly $300 million on Wednesday, up from $95 million a day earlier, as five-session withdrawals reached $1.44 billion.
items.articleText: BlackRock Bitcoin ETF outflows hit $2B over nine sessions US spot Bitcoin ETF outflows rose to nearly $300 million on Wednesday, up from $95 million a day earlier, as five-session withdrawals reached $1.44 billion. BlackRock’s spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF), the iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), recorded more than $2 billion in net outflows over nine consecutive trading sessions through Wednesday. Investors pulled a net $269.7 million from IBIT on Wednesday, accounting for about 90% of the day’s $300 million in net withdrawals across US spot Bitcoin ETFs, according to Farside Investors data. Grayscale’s Bitcoin Trust ETF (GBTC) recorded $39.1 million in net withdrawals, while the Morgan Stanley Bitcoin Trust ETF (MSBT) drew $9 million in net inflows. US spot Bitcoin ETFs posted nearly $1.44 billion in net withdrawals over five straight sessions. Wednesday’s increase followed three sessions of easing outflows. Crypto exchange Bitfinex said on Wednesday that slowing ETF outflows could be an early step toward a market floor, but were not enough on their own to establish a recovery. Bitfinex found that in the ETF outflow streaks it studied earlier this year, Bitcoin gained a median 6.4% over 10 trading sessions when the streaks ended with at least three consecutive sessions of net inflows. Bitcoin traded near $73,000 at the time of writing, down 8.5% over the past week, according to CoinGecko. In a Wednesday note shared with Cointelegraph, Laser Digital’s derivatives trading desk pointed to weak spot demand, a persistently negative Coinbase premium and large liquidations of leveraged long positions. The desk said Bitcoin barely rose during Monday’s rebound in the Nasdaq, which gained almost 3%. Related: Bitcoin hovers near $74K as stocks rise despite US bond yield rebound

items.titleTr: Oranges investigated after four girls die in suspected Uganda school poisoning
items.summaryTr: The girls started vomiting after eating oranges brought in by a fellow pupil - police are travelling to the village they came from.
items.articleText: Oranges investigated after four girls die in suspected Uganda school poisoning - Published Ugandan police are investigating the deaths of four pupils at a school in the capital Kampala which they suspect may be the result of poisoning. The four girls, aged between nine and 11 years, died on Tuesday. Three of the pupils died at home while the fourth passed away while receiving emergency treatment at a hospital. The head teacher at the school, Ta'aliim Primary School and Quran Memorisation Centre, has been arrested to assist with investigations. According to the school, eight pupils had eaten oranges shared by a fellow pupil. Five pupils, including the four who later died, started vomiting. The fifth is still in hospital. Post-mortem examinations are being carried out to determine the exact cause of death. A police spokesperson was quoted by local media as saying that detectives would visit the village where the oranges the pupils ate came from. The centre has been cordoned off as a crime scene. Ugandan media shared videos of grieving parents describing their children's final moments, with some accusing the school of failing to provide clear and timely information. The police have offered condolences to the bereaved families and affected community and say more information will be provided in due course. The tragedy comes at a time when concerns are mounting over health and safety conditions in schools across Uganda. Previous cases involving suspected contaminated food and exposure to harmful substances have left pupils hospitalised with symptoms including stomach pain, vomiting and breathing difficulties. The incidents have intensified calls for authorities to strengthen monitoring of school feeding schemes, improve hygiene standards and ensure safer learning environments for children. items.summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

items.titleTr: Here’s what happened in crypto today
items.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
items.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, Binance’s chief security officer described a fake job interview attack months before hackers used a similar tactic in the exchange’s $6.3 billion breach; OKX and NYSE parent ICE prepared to launch tokenized stock trading despite objections from dozens of major companies, and Barclays increased its holdings in BlackRock’s spot Bitcoin ETF by 48% in the third quarter. Binance CSO unwittingly foreshadowed $6.3B hack tactic months before attack Months before Binance lost $6.3 billion to a hack, its chief security officer described to Cointelegraph how a fake job interview could give attackers a foothold inside the exchange — closely resembling one of the entry methods later used against the exchange. During a July interview about Binance’s response to rising security threats, Jimmy Su told Cointelegraph that fake job interviews were “something we worry about a lot internally,” explaining how attackers could tailor a job opportunity to an employee before persuading them to run code as part of a technical assessment. “And once that gets executed, the device is compromised and then they can start harvesting credentials,” Su said, adding that attackers could then use that to penetrate further into the network. Su’s detailed warning about malicious coding assessments was not included in Cointelegraph’s July coverage, but takes on new significance following the biggest crypto exchange hack in history. OKXICE moves ahead with tokenized stocks as blue chips push back Crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) are set to launch tokenized stock trading on Nov. 23, despite objections from 67 companies to having their shares listed and warnings from Nasdaq that trading across disconnected platforms could fragment liquidity. The venture, known as OKXICE, will operate under the US Securities and Exchange Commission’s temporary Innovation Exemption and offer eligible US customers round-the-clock trading. Under the exemption, venues must give companies a chance to object before listing shares tokenized by an unaffiliated third party. JPMorgan Chase, McDonald’s, SpaceX and Coca-Cola were among the companies that objected. Tokenized stocks are blockchain-based tokens that represent company shares or track their price. The rights they carry depend on how they are structured. The distributed value of tokenized stocks and ETFs reached $3.88 billion on Nov. 11, up 13.4% over 30 days. In comments to Cointelegraph, former New York governor and OKXICE co-chair Andrew Cuomo said investors would have “the same rights, protections and ownership that come with the underlying shares.” Barclays boosts BlackRock Bitcoin ETF stake 48% as banks expand holdings Barclays reported holding 3.94 million shares in BlackRock’s spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) at the end of the third quarter, up 48% from the previous quarter. The position in the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) was worth about $187 million on Sept. 30, up from $88.5 million for 2.66 million shares on June 30, according to Barclays’ Friday Form 13F filing. “Early readings suggest longer-term holders make up a growing share of the spot bitcoin ETF investor base,” Bitwise analyst Camran Khosravi told Cointelegraph, pointing to increased bank exposure, including at Citigroup. Citigroup reported a new position worth about $119 million in the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC). Its reported IBIT holdings also rose 50% to about 521,000 shares, from 347,000 at the end of June. The filings offer an early indication of changing institutional Bitcoin ETF ownership, with more major banks and hedge funds yet to disclose their third-quarter positions. Institutional investment managers have until Monday to file their third-quarter holdings reports.

The position in the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) was worth about $187 million on Sept. 30, up from $88.5 million for 2.66 million shares on June 30, according to Barclays’ Friday Form 13F filing. “Early readings suggest longer-term holders make up a growing share of the spot bitcoin ETF investor base,” Bitwise analyst Camran Khosravi told Cointelegraph, pointing to increased bank exposure, including at Citigroup. Citigroup reported a new position worth about $119 million in the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC). Its reported IBIT holdings also rose 50% to about 521,000 shares, from 347,000 at the end of June. The filings offer an early indication of changing institutional Bitcoin ETF ownership, with more major banks and hedge funds yet to disclose their third-quarter positions. Institutional investment managers have until Monday to file their third-quarter holdings reports.

items.title: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
items.articleText: Release Number 9324-26 CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers November 09, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced eight orders filing and settling charges against Michael Talento, Anthony Tyler Williams, Quillan Roberto Black, Christopher Williams, Michael Levi Peters, Jordan Taylor Morgan, Lewis Matthew Neal, and Tyler Evan MacKechnie for acting as unregistered associated persons of unregistered foreign introducing brokers. According to the orders, the introducing brokers engaged in the solicitation of orders for off-exchange leveraged or margined retail foreign currency and retail commodities transactions with U.S. customers who were not eligible contract participants. The respondents solicited those customers without registering as associated persons of the introducing brokers, as required. Under the orders, the respondents must cease and desist from engaging in their illegal conduct. They also are barred for two years from registering with the Commission in any capacity or acting as a principal, agent, or employee of any CFTC registrant. Each order also recognizes the penalty the respondent owes in a related Securities and Exchange Commission proceeding. These orders relate to a prior Commission order sanctioning Netrios LP Ltd. and Red Acre Ltd. for facilitating illegal off-exchange commodity transactions with U.S. customers. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9263-26] The SEC has filed and settled charges against the respondents based on the same underlying conduct. The CFTC thanks the SEC for its assistance. -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
items.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

items.articleText: Release Number 9322-26 CFTC Staff Addresses Use of Trust Companies for Daily Settlements November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s Division of Clearing and Risk today issued a no-action letter addressing whether derivatives clearing organizations may use trust companies to conduct daily settlements with clearing members. According to the letter, a derivatives clearing organization may use a trust company for daily settlements if it treats the trust company as it would a settlement bank under applicable CFTC requirements. -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
items.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
items.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
items.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
items.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-

items.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
items.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-
